sites.evidence_type: N-terminal HA epitope; parallel surface-display screen
sites.functional_impact_measured: Surface immunostaining PME 922.3 ± 86.1 (HA immunostaining, Tedman deep receptor scanning)
sites.rationale: Experimentally validated N-terminal HA epitope insertion (after signal-peptide cleavage where present); surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in Tedman et al. deep receptor scanning.

sources.citation: Tedman et al., Efficient experimental characterization of the GPCRome via deep receptor scanning, Nat Commun 2026 (bioRxiv 2025.09.19.677468, PMC12458215)
sources.claim: N-terminal HA epitope inserted per receptor; surface expression read out by HA immunostaining in a pooled GPCRome deep-receptor-scanning screen.

sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Anti-FLAG immunofluorescence confirmed cell-surface display of the tagged receptor (L3). The PRESTO-TANGO construct was used in a beta-arrestin recruitment (TANGO) functional assay across 320 GPCRs, demonstrating that the N-terminal FLAG does not prevent receptor trafficking or signaling.
sites.rationale: L2 explicitly states that the PRESTO-TANGO HTR1D construct carries a FLAG tag at the N-terminus (5′-end) after a cleavable signal sequence, placing the tag on the extracellular face. HTR1D is a GPCR with a single extracellular terminus (residues 1–38; TM1 begins at residue 39, giving 38 aa of clearance, well above the ≥3 aa minimum), so the junction is unambiguously a prepend before residue 1 (M). L3 corroborates surface display by anti-FLAG immunofluorescence, and L1 (PMID 11854302) independently reports a FLAG-tagged 5HT1D construct in HEK-293 cells, consistent with the same N-terminal topology-derived position. No residue number is cited in any clip, so position_evidence is topology_derived. PRESTO-TANGO full-length HTR1D construct (PMC4424118) carries an exogenous cleavable signal sequence followed by a FLAG epitope tag at the 5′-end (N-terminus) of the receptor to enable surface-expression monitoring. After signal-peptide cleavage the FLAG is displayed at the extracellular N-terminus of the membrane-anchored receptor. No specific residue number is named in the clip; HTR1D has exactly one extracellular terminus (residues 1–38, 38 aa before TM1 at residue 39), so the junction is topology-derived as a prepend before residue 1.

sources.claim: At the 5′-end, we included a cleavable signal sequence to promote membrane localization 23 and a FLAG epitope tag in order to be able to monitor cell surface expression by immunohistochemistry.

literature_notes: Three ledger lines were evaluated. L2 and L3 (PMC4424118, PRESTO-TANGO) together provide the strongest evidence: L2 explicitly names the N-terminal FLAG placement and L3 confirms surface expression by immunofluorescence and functional use in the TANGO assay. L1 (PMID 11854302) reports a FLAG-tagged 5HT1D construct used for co-immunoprecipitation but states no tag position; because HTR1D has exactly one extracellular terminus, topology_derived reasoning places it at the same N-terminal site — it does not add a second independent site. No ledger line supports any insertion in ECL1 (98–112), ECL2 (177–196), or ECL3 (327–337), so no internal sites are proposed. The intracellular C-terminus (360–377) is not a surface site and is not proposed.
